4. Respondent No.4 entered appearance by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the petitioner, the Superintendent of the Madrasha, was not performing his function with due diligence and that he never became the victim of conspiracy. It has been contended that in view of the allegations brought against him he was suspended on 21-1-1995. Challenging the order of suspension the petitioner preferred Writ Petition No.2104 of 2001 before the High Court Division. The Rule issued in connection with the said writ petition ultimately was discharged on 8-8-2005. It has further been contended that before holding inquiry the Inquiry Committee duly informed the petitioner. Accordingly, on the date of enquiry he appeared and endorsed his signature in the attendance sheet on 6- 12-95 before Inquiry Committee. It has also been contended that the inquiry Committee considered all the documents supplied by the petitioner and accordingly, submitted its report. Moreover, the petitioner was duly informed by the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Bangladesh Madrasha Education Board vide memo No. Shongsta/3/20 dated 16-1-2002 and memo No. Shongsta/4/14 dated 14-2-2002 respectively with direction to appear before the said Committee with necessary papers in support of the case of the petitioner. The petitioner duly appeared before the said Committee and after hearing him and examining all papers it had rightly approved the proposal of the Managing Committee for dismissal of the petitioner. The said order was duly communicated to the petitioner vide Memo No. Shaongstha 54/7/A 8(implementation) 2003 dated 28-7-2003 (Annexure-D). It has further been stated that in the meeting of the Managing Committee of the Madrasha dated 15-11-1994 it had been decided in presence of the petitioner that he would give accounts of income and expenditure of the Madrasha. The petitioner prayed for time accordingly one month time was allowed. In spite of making repeated request by the Managing Committee the petitioner did not give any accounts of income and expenditure of the Madrasha properly. Due to his failure in performing the duties, to keep the accounts properly and also due to misappropriation of Madrasha fund the Managing Committee vide decision dated 21-1-1995 suspended him from his service temporarily. The petitioner was present in the said meeting endorsing his signature at serial No.5. In the said meeting it was also decided that an audit team would be formed consisting of 3 (three) members. Accordingly, an audit team was formed who did the audit of the accounts of the Madrasha and submitted report on 13-2-1995. Subsequently, the Chairman of the Managing Committee of the Madrasha issued notice No. 168/95 dated 25-2-1995 directing the petitioner to show cause as to why he should not be dismissed from service in accordance with the service rules on the charge of misappropriation of fund, misuse of power, negligence and disobedience to higher authority. The petitioner on receipt of the said notice duly replied on 12-3-95. The reply having been found not satisfactory as such another inquiry committee was formed consisting of 3 (three) members, the Thana Project Officer Mymensingh (Sadar), the Assistant Co-operative Officer, Mymensingh Sadar and one Assistant Teacher of the Madrasha. On 6- 12-1995 the Inquiry Committee inquired into the charges brought against the petitioner in his presence and 6 (six) others. After completion of enquiry the Inquiry Committee submitted its report vide memo No. FSSP/sho-Moy/95/115(2) dated 31-12- 1995. Challenging the suspension order dated 21-1-1995 the petitioner instituted other Class Suit No. 49 of 1996 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh for declaration that the suspension order was illegal. Subsequently, the suit was re-numbered as OC. Suit No.13 of 1997 on transfer to the Court of Assistant Judge; Dhubaura, Mymensingh. The said suit was ultimately dismissed on contest vide judgment and decree dated 29-5-1997. Challenging the same the petitioner preferred other Class Appeal No. 167 of 1997 in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh. The Appeal was transferred to the Court of Sub-Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh who after hearing the contenting parties dismissed the same vide judgment and decree dated 31-8-1999. After disposal of the suit the Chairman of the Managing Committee of the Madrasha vide notice No.429 dated 20-7-1997 directed the petitioner to show cause within 7 (seven) days in respect of the charges so brought against him. The reply so given by the petitioner was found not satisfactory and upon considering the inquiry report and the reply of the petitioner the Managing Committee vide resolution dated 6-12- 2000 decided to dismiss the petitioner from service subject to approval of the respondent No.1. Accordingly, the proposal was sent to the Board on 20-2-2000. Suppressing all those facts the petitioner had preferred writ petition No.2104 of 2001 and the Rule issued therein was ultimately discharged on contest on 8-8-2005. Bringing the same issue the petitioner again filed the instant writ petition hence; it is liable to be discharged being hit by the doctrine of res-judicata. 

 8. So far suspension order is concerned, the petitioner challenging the same instituted other Class Suit No.49 of 1996 re-numbered as other Class Suit No. 13 of 1997 on transfer before the Court of Assistant Judge, Dhubaura, Mymensingh. The suit was ultimately dismissed on contest vide judgment and decree dated 19-5-1997. Challenging which the petitioner had preferred other Class Appeal No. 167 of 1997 in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh, which was ultimately heard by the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, (now, the joint District Judge) 3rd Court Mymensingh. The said appeal was also dismissed vide judgment and decree dated 31-8-1999. From Annexure 1 to the affidavit- in-opposition it appears that challenging the suspension order the petitioner also filed writ petition No. 2104 of 2001 before this court and obtained Rule without disclosing the facts regarding filing of the suit and appeal and its dismissal.
